top.line: Where investment in sgit should go: the tool, a hub for vaults, or open core. The answer is the hub, with the deck as a vault.
top.para: Platform history says the network beats the host, registries struggle alone, hosting is where open source gets paid, and the hub of public work is the moat. Git is strained by agents and capital is following. The recommendation is SGitHub, with the format open; the deck, thesis, plans and evidence are a public vault forked per investor.

in-short.line: The question, the history, why now, where sgit is, the gap, the answer, and the deck as a vault.
in-short.para: Three candidates for investment; platform history favours the hub of public work; Anthropic's Scion and Entire's seed show the moment; sgit has 99 releases and most of Git parity, but no paying customer of its own yet. Fund the hub, keep the format open, sell self-host support, and fork the deck for each investor.

question.line: If money goes into sgit, should it go to the tool, a hub for vaults, or open core?
question.para: The three candidates are sgit and its open format; SGitHub, a hosted hub to share, fork, discover and run vaults; and open core in the GitLab style. The author runs several versions at once, so the question is real, and declares a stake in the answer.

why-now.line: Anthropic replaced Git for its monorepo, and startups building version control for agents are being funded.
why-now.para: Merges at Anthropic went from about 2,500 to more than 30,000 a day, and Scion replaced Git, though Anthropic says it is not for general use. Entire raised a $60M seed; GitButler, Pierre and Graphite also drew money. None encrypt the work from the host or treat the work itself as the unit.

history.line: Sixteen platforms: the network beats the host, registries struggle, hosting pays, the hub is the moat.
history.para: SourceForge sold for about $20M and GitHub for $7.5B. npm and Docker Hub struggled to monetise. MongoDB, Supabase and Vercel turned open source into hosted revenue; IBM bought Red Hat, HashiCorp and Confluent; Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.93B. Open-source companies raise Series A at 1.6 times their closed peers.

answer.line: Fund SGitHub, keep the format open, and sell self-host support as the bridge to revenue.
answer.para: The tool alone is Git's story, with no company; open core needs a proprietary tier sgit rules out. The hub is where the network forms: public vaults with read keys, vault apps that run when opened, agents as users, and a host that cannot read its users' work, which they can always leave.

state.line: 99 releases since March, 5,032 test functions, most of Git parity done and seven more designs to build.
state.para: PyPI shows 99 releases up to 0.26.5; the repository has 1,757 commits and cli.sgit.ai lists 174 commands. The October burst came from a real vault. Line-level merge and partial commits are on dev; signing, renames, blame, bisect, grep, cherry-pick, hooks, rebase and worktree are designed, at about 36 to 40 days.

use.line: Real production use, mostly our own, and no paying customer of sgit itself yet.
use.para: A 2.7 GB vault clones in 95 seconds instead of nearly 14 minutes; ten agents share one vault; the RiskMandate team runs on vaults; health-related projects use them, with OmKneeHealth public. Ruflo merged an sgit pull request. Against that: no paying customer, downloads are not users, no real keys in the PKI register.

evolution.line: The ideas came first: the vault in February, read keys and PKI in October, the hub next.
evolution.para: From SG/Send's first commit on 8 February, through the CLI in March and PyPI on 20 March, to read keys, mirrors and policy on 7 October, PKI on 10 October, pack mode on 22 October and byte-range clones on 27 October. The hub is the next step on the same line.

vault.line: The deck is a vault: a 20-slide app with its PDF, thesis, three plans, data, articles and a personalise script.
vault.para: Opening the vault runs the deck; cloning it brings the thesis, plans A to C, sourced data, the articles behind the numbers, ideas for investors, and personalise.py, which forks a copy per investor so they see what changed. The ask is left blank until the founder states it.

investors.line: Ideas to create interest and pick investors, each one the product selling itself.
investors.para: A write-only lane for investors to leave a note; a data room that is a vault their agent can read; cloning one folder of a 2.7 GB vault in the meeting; three questions about open source, agents and a public pitch; and checking early for conflicts with funds in Entire, GitButler or Pierre.

limits.line: A thesis, not a forecast; SGitHub is not built; valuations are other companies'; the author has a stake.
limits.para: Milestones and plans are proposals for discussion. The roadmap names SGitHub as a future product. Some valuations are labelled estimates, and the Hugging Face deal is pending. Most production evidence is the author's own companies' use.

sources.line: Anthropic's Scion post, PyPI, the CLI repository and roadmap, cli.sgit.ai, sgit.ai/investors, and the vault's data.
sources.para: Every platform figure is in the vault's platforms.json with its URL, quote and confidence label; the Linux Foundation study is from August 2025. Research was done by this site's agent, under the author's direction.
